newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to fill gap in Bulgaria's financing.
newsitem.headline: EU to fill gap in Bulgaria's financing.

text.p: The European Commission announced on Wednesday it would propose a balance of payments aid package of up to 250 million Ecus ($285 million) for Bulgaria to help fill the gap left by an IMF standby loan.

Bulgaria's Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Bozhkov told a news conference after a meeting of the Group of 24 richest countries that the aid, along with bilateral pledges, meant that Sofia now expected $400 million extra to get back on its feet.
It would allow Sofia to really launch an economic restructuring package. "With this support that we will be getting, we will be able to service our debts in 1997-1998," he said.
The G-24 meeting was called to help ease the effects of Bulgaria's tough reform programme on its already impoverished people.

The extra aid was welcome "because we are starting a very ambitious programme...The people of Bulgaria are tired of reform anticipation, they want reform. If they only see the bad side there can be problems," Bozhkov said.

A statement issued after the G-24 meeting said the country's caretaker government "has shown strong commitment to implement a bold macro economic stabilisation and structural reform despite exceptionally difficult circumstances."
But the meeting urged Bulgaria to keep its economic programme on track and implement it within the agreed time frame.
The Commission also said it would propose an additional targeted social and structural reform assistance of up to 40 million Ecus under the EU's Phare programme.
Bozhkov said he was satisfied, but only "quite", with the results.
Bulgaria had been looking to the EU and other lenders to fill the gap of about $500 million in funding needs for the reform programme.
A European Commission official told the news conference the new EU aid would be on the same conditions as those which apply to the IMF package.
